title: Westbrook High Rising
premise: Jonah Underhill, Westbrook High's statistician, has spent three years documenting how the school's celebrated basketball dynasty is propped up by grade-fixing orchestrated by Coach Renner and her best friend Marcus, the star point guard. When a semester-long civics project pairs her with her nemesis—Marcus's sharp-tongued sister Delia—the two uncover evidence that threatens to unravel not just the team but the friendship and belonging Jonah has quietly built from the sidelines. As graduation looms and the district closes in, Jonah must choose between exposing the truth that will destroy Marcus and protecting the only community she's ever had. She testifies before the school board in the final chapter, losing Marcus's friendship but finding an honest place for herself, as Westbrook's championship banner comes down and something truer begins to rise in its place.
about_author: Vesper Whitlock is a former small-town sports reporter who spent four seasons in the bleachers of high school gyms across the Midwest, collecting the stories nobody put in the box scores. She writes young adult novels about the quiet kids who see everything.

chapters.title: Forty-Seven Days
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Opening with her countdown calendar and meticulous stat notebooks, Jonah establishes her invisible role at Westbrook and her private suspicion that the team's perfect season doesn't add up. The emotional beat is weary resignation—she's counting down, not living.

chapters.title: Assigned Seats
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Mr. Okafor pairs her with Delia Reyes for the semester civics project on institutional accountability. Their first meeting in the library is all venom and stalemate, but Delia notices Jonah's stat notebook and asks one question Jonah can't dodge. The beat is reluctant, electric friction.

chapters.title: The Margin of Error
chapters.summary: Alternating Jonah and Delia POV. Comparing notes, they find impossible patterns: grades changed after eligibility deadlines, all routed through one office. Delia defends her brother at first, then goes silent. The beat is the vertigo of a shared secret taking shape.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Away Game
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the homecoming rally, Jonah watches Marcus bask in glory she now knows is borrowed, and realizes he once covered for her freshman year—complicating everything. Delia pulls her into an empty hallway: 'I found his old transcripts.' The beat is loyalty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: What the Banner Says
chapters.summary: Delia's POV. Delia confronts Marcus privately; he admits the grade-fixing started as Coach Renner's plan but that he let it happen to escape their neighborhood. Delia, shaken, hides it from Jonah—until Jonah finds the deleted attendance logs. The beat is betrayal compounding betrayal.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Coach Renner summons Jonah, offers her a paid assistant job and a college recommendation in exchange for the notebooks. Jonah pretends to consider, terrified. She and Delia reconcile in the empty gym, deciding to build the case together. The beat is fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Bribe and the Backup
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Renner, sensing exposure, has Jonah's locker searched and her project files wiped; Marcus, guilt-ridden, secretly restores the backups and leaves them anonymously for Delia. The girls realize someone inside is helping. The beat is fragile, unexpected alliance.

chapters.title: State Championship
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Championship night: Westbrook wins, the gym erupts, and Jonah stands at the scorers' table knowing the victory is a lie. Marcus, at the free-throw line, looks straight at her. The beat is triumph curdled—the town's joy built on what the girls are about to break.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The girls present the project—and the evidence—to the school board with Marcus testifying voluntarily against Renner. The gym community fractures; some call them traitors, others thank them. The beat is the climax: truth spoken aloud, costing everything at once.

chapters.title: Zero Days
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Graduation day. Renner is gone, the banner comes down, Marcus doesn't speak to Jonah but leaves a note: 'You were right. Thank you.' Delia and Jonah plan a student-led tutoring program for athletes. Jonah crosses the stage not invisible. The beat is grief and belonging, honestly earned.
